identity.name: Russian State
alt_names: Supreme Ruler of the Russian State

land.text: "the regions of Siberia": the Omsk Provisional Siberian Government (established 30 June 1918, power transferred 3 November 1918)

predecessors.note: The Omsk government of Siberia; no Cliopatria row, no dossier yet.

land.text: the Samara government (Komuch, set up 8 June 1918) whose People's Army was merged into the combined forces on 28 September 1918

predecessors.note: No Cliopatria row, no dossier yet.

land.text: the Provisional Regional Government of the Urals formed at Yekaterinburg on 25 August 1918

predecessors.note: No Cliopatria row, no dossier yet.

land.text: Omsk and Western Siberia (Red Army 14 November 1919), the Urals (Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk in July 1919), later Irkutsk

successors.note: Irkutsk passed from the Political Centre to a Bolshevik military committee on 20 January 1920, after the state had ended.

land.text: Kolchak's decree of 4 January 1920 gave Semyonov "the whole civil and military power on the territory of Russia eastern outskirts"

successors.note: Semyonov's Chita regime, 16 January to 28 October 1920; no dossier yet. It was followed by the Far Eastern Republic.

capitals.name: Ufa
capitals.note: The Directory formed in Ufa in September 1918; the page does not use the word capital.

capitals.name: Omsk
capitals.note: "The government moved from Ufa to Omsk" on 9 October 1918; Omsk was evacuated on 14 November 1919 (Alexander Kolchak page). Kolchak left for Irkutsk by rail on 13 November 1919.

minus.text: the regions of Siberia (Provisional Siberian Government, Omsk) with the Urals, Ufa, Orenburg and Samara-Syzran brought under the Ufa Directory; the Far East and Transbaikal are not included (nominal claim only)
Samara and Syzran, abandoned 8 and 3 October 1918 (ledger /3 and /2)

correction.text: the Russian State's land at the end of 1918: the September 1918 shape (Siberia, the Urals, Ufa, Orenburg, Samara-Syzran) without Samara and Syzran, which the Directory forces abandoned to the Red Army on 8 and 3 October; the compiler checks a keyframe at the end of its start year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for this state; its Russian Republic shape (17.9 M km2 in 1918) spans all of Russia. The page gives no area figure. The union is the Siberian Government's Siberia plus the Urals, Ufa, Orenburg and the Samara-Syzran Volga bank held by the combined forces until October. Samara and Syzran were abandoned on 8 and 3 October 1918, so they leave this shape in the ledger within the year. The Far East and Transbaikal were not controlled from Omsk. [fx-21 2026-11-01: the correction now subtracts Samara (100 km) and Syzran (60 km), lost in October 1918 by ledger /2 and /3 (Russian State page: 'October 3, 1918: Syzran was abandoned', 'October 8, 1918: Samara was abandoned'); a keyframe is compared with the ledger at the end of its start year, and without this the compiler re-added 155 cells the ledger had just given up.]

correction.text: the Russian State's land at the end of 1919: the Yenisei (Krasnoyarsk) region, which the Red 5th Army took on 7 January 1920 (Great Siberian Ice March page). Omsk fell on 14 November, Tomsk on 20 December, Irkutsk went to the Political Centre in late December (ledger /21); the spring-1919 peak (Perm, Ufa, the Udmurt towns, Altai, the Steppe) is carried by the ledger gains of December 1918 to April 1919 and its losses from June 1919

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the spring-1919 peak after Perm (24 December 1918), Ufa (14 March) and the Udmurt towns (April). Ledger losses take Ufa (9 June), Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk (July) and then Omsk (14 November) out of it within the year. The Alexander Kolchak page says "Kolchak's territories covered over 300,000 km2 and held around 7 million people": the first figure cannot be right for Siberia and the Urals (the union drawn here is several million km2), so the keyframe follows the named units, not the figure. The Far East ("Russian power there was almost nominal") and Transbaikal are a vassal tint in the ledger, not part of this shape. [fx-21 2026-11-01: the correction is now the end-of-1919 shape. The compiler compares a keyframe with the ledger at the end of its start year, and this one-year keyframe was the spring peak: after the ledger's 1919 losses (Ufa, the Urals, Omsk, Western Siberia, Irkutsk) it re-added 11,758 cells (Krasnoyarsk 8,656, Irkutsk 3,102) and claimed 13,423 that the RSFSR (11,577) and Alash Autonomy (1,844) held. Sources: Great Siberian Ice March page (Tomsk 20 December 1919, Krasnoyarsk 7 January 1920), Alexander Kolchak page (Omsk 14 November, Political Centre in Irkutsk in late December).]

correction.text: Grigory Semyonov received authority in the Eastern Fringe pending Denikin's instructions (decree of 4 January 1920)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1-4 January 1920 only: after the fall of Omsk and the Irkutsk rising the state held only what Kolchak's last decree passed to Semyonov, "the Eastern Fringe". The Alexander Kolchak page puts Irkutsk under the Political Centre from late December 1919.

region.text: the regions of Siberia (Provisional Siberian Government, Omsk) with the Urals, Ufa, Orenburg and Samara-Syzran brought under the Ufa Directory; the Far East and Transbaikal are not included (nominal claim only)

ledger.note: 1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state". The state starts on the Omsk government's Siberia, the Urals government's Urals and the Ufa-Samara-Orenburg area held by the combined forces; the page names provinces, not a boundary.

minus.text: the gazetteer's Urals: the Sverdlovsk (Yekaterinburg), Chelyabinsk, Orenburg, Bashkortostan, Udmurt and Perm' oblasts
Kungur and Perm, taken only on 21 and 24 December 1918 (ledger /10)

region.text: the Urals and Orenburg that the RSFSR dossier loses to this state in September 1918 (its ledger /11), less Perm and Kungur

ledger.note: 1918, September: the Urals pass to the new state with the Ufa Conference. Eastern Front (Russian Civil War) page: 'In May 1918, soldiers of the Czechoslovak Legion revolted against the Bolsheviks in Chelyabinsk'; 'a Provisional Regional Government of the Urals in Yekaterinburg on 25 August 1918'; the Directory 'was created by the Ufa Conference on 23 September 1918'. The page gives no boundary; the region is the RSFSR event's (its Urals region also covers Bashkortostan and Udmurt; both dossiers' 1918 keyframes agree, the RSFSR's holding none of the six oblasts at the end of 1918 and this state's all of them). [fx-21 review 2026-11-01: new event, mirror of russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic /ledger/11. The compiler applies that loss only as this dossier's gain when this dossier has any 1918 gain from the RSFSR (it has: Kungur and Perm, ledger /10), so the loss moved nothing; the found claim loses RSFSR-held cells under rule R2 (the RSFSR is this state's successor), and the 1918 keyframe still had to add them (Sverdlovsk 687, Chelyabinsk 284, Bashkortostan 234, Orenburg 177 in the last compile). Perm and Kungur stay with the December event.]

region.text: Syzran, abandoned 3 October 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 3 October: Syzran abandoned to the Red Army ("October 3, 1918: Syzran was abandoned").

region.text: Samara, abandoned 8 October 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 8 October: Samara, the Komuch capital, abandoned ("October 8, 1918: Samara was abandoned").
1918, 9 October: the government moves from Ufa to Omsk because of the Red Army's approach.

region.text: the Volga-Ural front between the combined Eastern Russian forces and the Red Army, Syzran and Samara to Ufa, Orenburg and Perm

ledger.note: 1918, October: the Volga-Ural front opens as Boldyrev organises three fronts (Western, South-Western, Siberian) and the Red Army takes the Volga bank; zone drawn from the cities the page names.

region.text: "the regions of Siberia"

ledger.note: 1918, 3 November: every minister of the Omsk Provisional Siberian Government signs the transfer of power to the All-Russian Government at Omsk. [fx-21 2026-11-01: type changed from merge to gain. The compiler reads a merge whose counterpart has no dossier as the state giving up its own land (here it released 20,662 cells of Siberia in November 1918 and the 1918 keyframe then had to add 22,722 back); the region is already inside the found event, so this event now dates the transfer and takes only land nobody holds. Dated sentence re-checked on the Provisional Siberian Government page: 'The transfer of power to the Provisional All-Russian Government was signed on November 3, 1918, in Omsk'; Russian State page: 4 November the regional governments are told to dissolve and the Council of Ministers is formed on the basis of the Siberian government's ministries.]

region.text: regional, national and Cossack governments of eastern Russia, the Ural and Orenburg ones among them

ledger.counterpart: regional, national and Cossack governments of eastern Russia
ledger.note: 1918, 4 November: the government orders all regional, national and Cossack governments in eastern Russia dissolved, concentrating authority in the Directory. [fx-21 2026-11-01: type changed from merge to gain. The compiler reads a merge whose counterpart has no dossier as the state giving up its own land (here it released 20,662 cells of Siberia in November 1918 and the 1918 keyframe then had to add 22,722 back); the region is already inside the found event, so this event now dates the transfer and takes only land nobody holds. Dated sentence re-checked on the Provisional Siberian Government page: 'The transfer of power to the Provisional All-Russian Government was signed on November 3, 1918, in Omsk'; Russian State page: 4 November the regional governments are told to dissolve and the Council of Ministers is formed on the basis of the Siberian government's ministries.]

1918, 18 November: Kolchak's coup; the Council of Ministers at Omsk "assumed full power and conferred it on Kolchak as Supreme Leader", ending the Directory; the state and its territory continue as the Russian State under the Supreme Ruler.

region.text: Transbaikalia under ataman Semyonov, a "buffer state east of Lake Baikal under Cossack control" (Alexander Kolchak page)

ledger.note: 1918, 18 December: Kolchak orders military districts formed, among them a Far East district at Khabarovsk, but "Russian power there was almost nominal" and the Japanese corps held the ports. Transbaikal east of Baikal is treated as a Cossack buffer, a client tint, not Omsk territory. The pages give no date for Semyonov's acknowledgement of Omsk; the year is the district order's. [Reviewer eu-17-x: counterpart was russian-eastern-outskirts, which the Eastern Okraina page dates from 16 January 1920, after this state ended.]

region.text: Kungur on 21 December and Perm on 24 December 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 21-24 December: the Siberian Army takes Kungur (21 December) and Perm (24 December) from the Reds.

region.text: Ufa, occupied 14 March 1919

ledger.note: 1919, 14 March: the Western Army occupies Ufa ("The White forces took Ufa in March 1919", Alexander Kolchak page).

region.text: Sarapul, Votkinsk and Izhevsk (Siberian Army); Belebey, Birsk, Bugulma and Buguruslan (Western Army), April 1919

ledger.note: 1919, April: the Siberian Army takes Sarapul, Votkinsk and Izhevsk; the Western Army takes Belebey, Birsk, Bugulma (10 April) and Buguruslan and approaches Samara.

region.text: Ufa, retaken 9 June 1919

ledger.note: 1919, 9 June: "The Red Army retook Ufa" (the Russian State page dates the lost battle for Ufa 25 May to 19 June, with the Western Army retreating to Chelyabinsk); in June Red forces broke through the Urals.

region.text: Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk, left in July 1919

ledger.note: 1919, July: the Siberian Army "withdrew to the Trans-Urals, leaving Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk" (the Alexander Kolchak page dates the capture of Chelyabinsk 25 July 1919).

union.text: the Urals ridge and both slopes left with the withdrawal to the Trans-Urals

region.text: the Urals and Bashkir lands taken in the spring offensive, the Sverdlovsk and Chelyabinsk oblasts and the Urals region left with the withdrawal to the Trans-Urals

ledger.note: 1919, summer: the Urals west of the Trans-Urals line (Perm, Kungur, the Udmurt towns, Orenburg approaches) pass to the Reds with the retreat. Bridging: the pages date only Ufa (9 June), Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk (July) and the withdrawal "to the Trans-Urals"; Perm, Izhevsk and Sarapul are not dated as lost. [fx-21 2026-11-01: the Urals region added to the region (RSFSR /20 mirrors it). The circles around Perm, Izhevsk, Sarapul and Votkinsk left about 1,330 cells of the Urals region with the state to the end of 1919. Russian State page: April 1919 'As a result of the general offensive, the whole of the Ural was occupied'; June-July the Siberian army 'withdrew to the Trans-Urals', 'Ekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk were left'.] [fx-21 2026-11-01: the Sverdlovsk and Chelyabinsk oblasts added as well, the same two the RSFSR dossier takes from the state in September 1918 (/11); the 100 km circles of /13 left 584 and 182 of their cells with the state. Russian State page: 'Ekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk were left' in July 1919.]

region.text: the Volga-Ural front

ledger.note: 1919, July: the Volga-Ural front ends as the Siberian Army withdraws to the Trans-Urals and the Western Army to Chelyabinsk and beyond.

region.text: the Tobol and Ishim front before Omsk, August-November 1919

ledger.note: 1919, August-October: the 1st and 2nd Siberian armies join the Tobolsk offensive; in mid-October the Reds break through on the Tobol (Alexander Kolchak page). Zone from the cities the pages name.

region.text: Omsk, taken 14 November 1919

ledger.note: 1919, 14 November: Omsk is evacuated and the Red Army takes it without serious resistance; Kolchak had left for Irkutsk on 13 November with the gold reserve.

region.text: the Tobol and Ishim front

ledger.note: 1919, November: the Tobol-Omsk front ends with the fall of Omsk; the White forces fall back "in a disorganised mass" toward Transbaikalia.

region.text: Western Siberia, Altai and the Steppe

ledger.note: 1919, November-December: the rest of Western Siberia (Tomsk, Novosibirsk), Altai and the Steppe are lost as "the Eastern Front collapsed; remnants retreated to Transbaikalia". Great Siberian Ice March page: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919"; the pages date neither Novosibirsk, the Altai nor the Steppe (bridging). [fx-21 2026-11-01: Krasnoyarsk taken out of this event and given its own event of 7 January 1920 (below): the same page has the Red 5th Army take Krasnoyarsk on 7 January 1920, after the government's last decree of 4 January, and the RSFSR dossier's year-end 1919 keyframe still leaves Krasnoyarsk outside Soviet land.]

region.text: Irkutsk under the Political Centre

ledger.note: 1919, late December: Irkutsk comes under a leftist group that forms the Political Centre; Kolchak, held by the Czechoslovak Legion, no longer commands it (he is dismissed 4 January 1920 and handed over 14 January).

region.text: the Eastern Fringe

ledger.note: 1920, 4 January: Kolchak's last decree transfers supreme power to Denikin and gives Semyonov "full military and civilian authority" in the Eastern Fringe; the buffer east of Baikal becomes Semyonov's own. [Reviewer eu-17-x: counterpart was russian-eastern-outskirts, which the Eastern Okraina page dates from 16 January 1920, after this state ended.]

region.text: the Yenisei (Krasnoyarsk) region

ledger.note: 1920, 7 January: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919 ... and Krasnoyarsk on 7 January 1920" (Great Siberian Ice March page); Kappel's army "was forced to find a route around the communist uprising in Krasnoyarsk". The city is the Russian State's last land west of Irkutsk at the end of 1919 and passes to the RSFSR three days after Kolchak's decree of 4 January (the successor land in identity.successors). Confidence 2: the page dates the Red army's entry, not who held the city on 31 December. [fx-21 2026-11-01: new event; mirror of russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic /ledger gain of 7 January 1920.]

region.text: the Eastern Fringe passed to Semyonov; Irkutsk to the Political Centre and then a Bolshevik military committee (20 January 1920)

ledger.note: 1920, 4 January: the Russian State ends with Kolchak's last decree; Kolchak was shot at Irkutsk on 6 or 7 February 1920, the Alexander Kolchak page giving both dates.

wars.name: Eastern Front of the Russian Civil War
wars.outcome: Bolshevik victory: Ufa and the Urals lost in June-July 1919, Omsk on 14 November 1919, the Kolchak government ended 4 January 1920.
wars.note: The pages date the front by city, not by line: the spring 1919 offensive reached Bugulma, Buguruslan and Sarapul; the Reds retook Ufa on 9 June.

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts and the nominal Far East claim; no treaty or survey line exists. The Samara-Syzran and Ufa lines are city-level readings.

sources.title: Russian State
sources.note: Founding 23 September 1918, Omsk move 9 October, 18 November coup, the 1919 front by date, 4 January 1920 decree; no area figure.

sources.title: Alexander Kolchak
sources.note: Fall of Omsk 14 November 1919, Irkutsk and the Political Centre, Ufa retaken 9 June 1919, Chelyabinsk 25 July 1919; the "over 300,000 km2" figure.

sources.title: Eastern Front (Russian Civil War)
sources.note: Thin: only the 1918 setup dates (Komuch 8 June, Provisional Siberian Government 23 June, Urals government 25 August, Directory 23 September, coup 18 November). The page said nothing of 1919.

sources.title: Provisional Siberian Government (Omsk)
sources.note: Established 30 June 1918, transferred power 3 November 1918; "the regions of Siberia".

sources.title: Eastern Okraina (Russian Eastern Outskirts)
sources.note: Semyonov's Chita regime 16 January to 28 October 1920; 4 January 1920 grant of power.

sources.title: Great Siberian Ice March
sources.note: Tomsk taken by the Red 5th Army on 20 December 1919, Krasnoyarsk on 7 January 1920; the communist uprising in Krasnoyarsk that Kappel's army had to bypass.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for this state: its Russian Republic shapes (1917-1919) cover all of Russia, Siberia and the Urals included, so the renderer must cut the White-held land out of that shape for the years above (events carry the month). Pages opened give no boundary, only cities and provinces; every region is a reading from them. The Alexander Kolchak page's "over 300,000 km2" is not credible and is not used. Not settled: (1) when Perm, Izhevsk and Sarapul fell; (2) the date of Novosibirsk (the Great Siberian Ice March page, opened 1 November 2026, dates Tomsk 20 December 1919 and Krasnoyarsk 7 January 1920); (3) the Far East: the Priamursky district existed on paper from 18 December 1918 but the Japanese corps held the ports (Siberian intervention page, Far Eastern Republic dossier). Other states this dossier needs from other groups: Komuch, Provisional Siberian Government, Provisional Regional Government of the Urals, Political Centre (Irkutsk), Russian Eastern Outskirts (16 January to 28 October 1920, Semyonov at Chita; the Eastern Okraina page was opened). The Czechoslovak Legion held the railway but no territory of its own on these pages. Gazetteer: all names used (Western Siberia, Urals, Transbaikal, admin1 and places) resolved at the time of writing.
